paper_metadata.title: Enhanced fill probability estimates in institutional algorithmic bond trading using statistical learning algorithms with quantum computers

summary: The paper studies a gate-based projected quantum feature map (PQFM) built from a 109-qubit Heisenberg-ansatz circuit on IBM ibm_torino hardware, using 4096 shots and Pauli Twirling + TREX mitigation. On a corporate bond RFQ fill-prediction task with 143,912 active-window RFQs and 16,000 sampled events/day, the best reported median test AUC reaches 0.97 ± 0.02 for the noisy hardware 'longer' circuit, versus about 0.60 ± 0.03 for noiseless simulation and about 0.63 ± 0.04 for classical inputs, but the paper does not demonstrate a practical quantum advantage in the Hoefler sense.

experiments.description: Projected quantum feature map (PQFM) generation using a Heisenberg-ansatz parameterized quantum circuit, evaluated on real corporate bond RFQ data via downstream classical fill-probability models; compared noiseless simulation vs IBM Heron hardware and two circuit variants ('shorter' and 'longer').

algorithm.variant: Projected Quantum Feature Map (PQFM) with Heisenberg ansatz

hyperparameters.measurement_observables: 1-local Pauli strings (X,Y,Z) on each qubit; some 2-local observables also included

algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initial state for each qubit; random seed 0

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 216 normalized classical event features are embedded into a 109-qubit Heisenberg-ansatz circuit; features are distributed over qubit indices and repetition indices, then measured as expectation values of Pauli observables to produce transformed features
problem_formulation.objective_function: Generate transformed market-event features x' = $M(U_α(x)|b0>) for downstream fill-probability estimation; no explicit optimization objective for the quantum circuit itself
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Heisenberg Hamiltonian H = sum_j J_j [X_j X_{j+1} + Y_j Y_{j+1} + 2 Z_j Z_{j+1}] (with Trotterized unitary evolution used for the feature map)

problem_instance.description: Corporate bond RFQ fill-probability estimation on real intraday algorithmic trading data; quantum feature generation is used as an offline transform for downstream classical models
problem_instance.dataset_name: HSBC proprietary corporate bond trading dataset

dataset_specification.description: European corporate bond market; RFQ events with binary fill labels; active trading window from July 24, 2024; 16k sampled events used for quantum feature generation and matching

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical features normalized by z-score, then transformed with 2r*tanh(1/3) to reduce outliers and fit quantum rotation range; event values scaled to [-1,1]; classical-quantum event matching via binning over feature range
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Backtesting with rolling time windows; out-of-sample AUC on future RFQs; comparisons across blinding windows of 0 to 4 trading days; median test AUC reported over model/hardware configurations; classical-quantum event matching evaluated at multiple resolutions

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise; decoherence and readout noise

implementation_details.classical_solver: scikit-learn Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, Feed-Forward Neural Network (downstream baselines)
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Normalization, tanh scaling, binning for event matching, rolling-window backtesting
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: AUC computation, median test AUC aggregation, classical-quantum event matching unification by mean over matched PQFM vectors

speedup_claims.conditions: out-of-sample test AUC on corporate bond RFQ fill-probability backtesting; best case with noisy quantum hardware-generated features
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports empirical uplift only; no theoretical or asymptotic speedup. Improvement is data-specific and not claimed to generalize.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large-scale fault-tolerant hardware would be required; the paper uses 109-qubit NISQ hardware with 4096 shots and error mitigation, but reports no complexity crossover analysis.
limiting_factors: Results are empirical AUC uplifts only, not a demonstrated end-to-end quantum advantage
Classical baselines remain strong and the paper does not show a quantum-only win on a practical benchmark with complexity analysis
NISQ noise and mitigation overhead dominate

notes: Hardware type and device name are explicitly stated as IBM Quantum ibm_torino with Heron r1 processor.
Number of qubits is explicitly stated as 109.
Circuit depth is not directly reported as a depth metric; inferred only that 'shorter' uses 1 block and 'longer' uses 2 blocks, but no exact depth count is given.
No asymptotic speedup is claimed; paper reports empirical AUC uplifts only, so speedup_order is none_proven.
The paper reports the Heisenberg Hamiltonian form and Trotterized unitary, but not a complexity analysis in Big-O terms.
The paper reports 109-qubit IBM Heron hardware (ibm_torino) with 4096 shots and Pauli Twirling + TREX mitigation.
It reports median test AUCs up to 0.97 ± 0.02 for the 'longer' hardware circuit, but this is an empirical feature-quality result rather than a proven quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Noiseless quantum simulation of the same PQFM/Heisenberg feature map on a classical simulator, used as a comparison against hardware-generated features for downstream fill-probability models.

algorithm.variant: Noiseless simulation of PQFM with Heisenberg ansatz

hyperparameters.measurement_observables: 1-local Pauli strings (X,Y,Z) on each qubit; some 2-local observables also included

algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initial state for each qubit; random seed 0

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same 216-feature-to-109-qubit PQFM mapping as hardware experiment, but executed on noiseless simulator
problem_formulation.objective_function: Generate transformed market-event features for downstream classical fill-probability estimation
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Heisenberg Hamiltonian with Trotterized unitary evolution

problem_instance.description: Same corporate bond RFQ fill-probability task, but using noiseless quantum simulation to generate features for comparison
problem_instance.dataset_name: HSBC proprietary corporate bond trading dataset
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same normalization, tanh scaling, and event matching protocol as hardware experiment
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Same backtesting/AUC methodology as hardware experiment

hardware.device_name: Qiskit Aer / Matrix Product State simulator

implementation_details.transpilation_target: Qiskit Aer / Estimator Primitive default settings
implementation_details.classical_solver: scikit-learn Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, Feed-Forward Neural Network (downstream baselines)

speedup_claims.conditions: noiseless quantum simulation baseline for downstream fill-probability models
speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim; simulation is used only as a comparison baseline and performs below classical inputs in reported AUC.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No advantage resources are established; this is a noiseless simulator baseline for the same 109-qubit gate-based circuit.
limiting_factors: Used only as a comparison baseline

notes: The paper explicitly states use of Matrix Product State simulation and Qiskit Aer Estimator Primitive.
No exact circuit depth is reported; only block counts for 'shorter' and 'longer' variants are given.
No asymptotic speedup claim is made; this is a comparison baseline for empirical feature quality.
The paper explicitly uses noiseless Qiskit Aer / Matrix Product State simulation of the same PQFM circuit.
Reported median test AUCs are around 0.60 ± 0.03 for the noiseless simulation, below the best hardware result.
